[[aou-proc-aou_fdi_t1_bringup_test]]
===== 4. `aou_fdi_t1_bringup_test`
Class `aou_fdi_t1_bringup_test` extends `uvm_test` (`uvm/tests/fdi/aou_fdi_t1_bringup_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* FDI bringup on the real DUT, RTL state encoding:
1. reset; the L2 agent runs the Adapter side of bringup (clk_req
handshake, inband_pres) with pl_clk_req released, so the DUT waits in
WAIT_PRESENCE until I_SW_ACTIVATE_START;
2. the DUT reaches Active (O_FDI_LINK_UP); empty flits with cancels,
poisoned cancelled halves and bubbles go to the DUT RX;
3. APB AOU_INIT.activate_start (0x08 bit 0) makes the core send an
ActivateReq, which the L1 monitor must capture on the DUT TX;
4. link events (Retrain, L1 entry/exit) and more flits.
The bringup model and the L1/L2 rule checks run throughout.

*Procedure.* The class's own `run_phase` (see the file).

*Pass criteria.* The base test's end-of-test checks: scoreboard drained, every declared expectation met, no unexpected `UVM_ERROR`/`UVM_FATAL`, the FDI checker clean; `scripts/check_run.py` judges the log against `expected_fail.yaml`.

|===

[[aou-proc-aou_fdi_t1_linkerror_spec_test]]
===== 6. `aou_fdi_t1_linkerror_spec_test`
Class `aou_fdi_t1_linkerror_spec_test` extends `aou_fdi_t1_bringup_test` (`uvm/tests/fdi/aou_fdi_t1_linkerror_spec_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* The bringup test with UCIe state encodings and a LinkError the protocol
layer raises itself (I_SW_LINKERROR_INJECT). UCIe r1.1 Table 8-2: the
protocol layer signals it on lp_linkerror, and the Adapter takes the link
to LinkError, then Reset, once it sees it. AOU_TOP has no lp_linkerror
(BUGS/002), so the bringup model reports FDI-M07. The Adapter then takes
the link down anyway, which brings the DUT back. Expected to fail
(expected_fail.yaml).

[[aou-proc-aou_fdi_t1_linkdown_spec_test]]
===== 7. `aou_fdi_t1_linkdown_spec_test`
Class `aou_fdi_t1_linkdown_spec_test` extends `aou_fdi_t1_bringup_test` (`uvm/tests/fdi/aou_fdi_t1_linkdown_spec_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* The bringup test with UCIe state encodings and every way the link goes
down (BUGS/001 item 4). NOP is ignored outside Reset (r1.1 Table 8-3), so:
1. teardown: I_SW_DEACTIVATE_START with the AoU core deactivated; the DUT
requests LinkReset or Disabled, the Adapter goes there and returns to
Reset on the DUT's Active request (§8.3.3.5/8.3.3.6); then bringup;
2. Adapter-initiated LinkReset, then Disabled: Link Status Down
(Table 8-2), so O_FDI_LINK_UP drops; Reset and bringup follow;
3. I_SW_LINKERROR_INJECT: lp_linkerror, the Adapter enters LinkError and
leaves it only on Active with lp_linkerror=0 (§8.3.3.7, FDI-R49).
The bringup model checks the DUT side throughout.

*Procedure.* The class's own `run_phase` (see the file).

*Rules named.* `FDI-R49`

*Pass criteria.* The base test's end-of-test checks: scoreboard drained, every declared expectation met, no unexpected `UVM_ERROR`/`UVM_FATAL`, the FDI checker clean; `scripts/check_run.py` judges the log against `expected_fail.yaml`.

[[aou-proc-aou_lp_mode_test]]
===== 15. `aou_lp_mode_test`
Class `aou_lp_mode_test` extends `aou_dp_base_test` (`uvm/tests/features/aou_lp_mode_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* TX low-power mode (plan 21.1-21.6; old F7). +lp_mode=0|1 and +lp_thr=T
(default: random 1..255 when +lp_mode=1) are programmed before activation;
aou_lp_mode_vseq counts idle flits from the L1 monitor. Traffic both ways
before and after the idle window, so credits are returned in LP mode (21.6).

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_lp_mode_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/aou_lp_mode_vseq.svh`):

TX low-power mode (FEAT-R08; BUGS/017 interim expectation). After traffic
drains and credits settle, counts the flits the DUT starts in an idle window
of WINDOW cycles:
- TX_LP_MODE=0: flits keep flowing, at least a quarter of the flit slots
(the L1 model's trdy holes take some);
- TX_LP_MODE=1, threshold 0: no flit;
- TX_LP_MODE=1, threshold T: at most one per max(T+1, flit cycles) plus one,
and at least half the rate of one flit T+1 cycles after each flit ends.
Then traffic runs again, so leaving the idle state is covered too.

*Rules named.* `FEAT-R08`

*Pass criteria.* The base test's end-of-test checks: scoreboard drained, every declared expectation met, no unexpected `UVM_ERROR`/`UVM_FATAL`, the FDI checker clean; `scripts/check_run.py` judges the log against `expected_fail.yaml`.

===== 16. `aou_dp_packing_test`
Class `aou_dp_packing_test` extends `aou_dp_base_test` (`uvm/tests/datapath/aou_dp_packing_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* Message packing (+dp_pack=wresp|crossflit|granule; plan 6.2, 6.9, 11.4,

flits, so messages cross flit boundaries into and out of the DUT.
- granule: 3-granule requests and 8-granule ReadData256 (reads of 32 B or
less) in both directions.

[[aou-proc-aou_link_event_test]]
===== 18. `aou_link_event_test`
Class `aou_link_event_test` extends `aou_base_test` (`uvm/tests/lifecycle/aou_link_event_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* FDI link events mid-traffic: Retrain, clk_req, L1, LinkError, LinkReset,
inband_pres (aou_link_event_vseq).

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_link_event_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/lifecycle/aou_link_event_vseq.svh`):

Adapter-initiated FDI link events while AoU is ENABLED and traffic runs
(fdi_enc=RTL). AoU's reaction is unspecified (BUGS/015); the interim
expectations are:
retrain, clk_wake  transparent: AoU stays ENABLED, no interrupt, every
transaction completes with correct data;
l1                 software deactivates first (MAS §7.3.6), the adapter
enters and leaves L1 (clk_req wake, Retrain, Active),
and the link activates again;
linkerror,         the link is lost mid-traffic; INT_REQ_LINKRESET may
link_reset,        rise; software resets AOU_CORE while the link is down,
inband_drop,       brings it up and activates again. In-flight
disabled           transactions are aborted by the reset (an M-port ID
mismatch interrupt is tolerated); all later traffic
must complete. Disabled is Adapter-initiated and needs
fdi_enc=SPEC, which the test selects for it.
Knobs: +event=retrain|clk_wake|l1|linkerror|link_reset|inband_drop|disabled|rand
(rand never picks disabled)

----
+loops +T1_TXN.
----

*Pass criteria.* The base test's end-of-test checks: scoreboard drained, every declared expectation met, no unexpected `UVM_ERROR`/`UVM_FATAL`, the FDI checker clean; `scripts/check_run.py` judges the log against `expected_fail.yaml`.

[[aou-proc-aou_attr_test]]
===== 25. `aou_attr_test`
Class `aou_attr_test` extends `aou_dp_base_test` (`uvm/tests/datapath/aou_attr_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* Stimulus for AXI request attributes across the link, both directions (plan
4.26-4.28, 5.24-5.26, 4.30): every transfer steps AxQOS 0-15, AxPROT 0-7 and
the legal AxCACHE encodings, separately for writes and reads
(+dp_attr_sweep), and the remote die puts a random PROF (FLEX[11:0]) in half
its AXI messages. The env's aou_t1_attr_chk checks the attributes on both
ends of the link and FLEX 0 from the DUT, the scoreboard the data (FLEX the
DUT receives must be ignored; it has no USER ports), and xfer_cov.attr_cg
shows every value was carried. FLEX[15:12] (v0.7 PROFEXTLEN) stays 0,
BUGS/027.

----
+attr_excl=1 (plan 4.25, 5.23) adds the exclusive rounds of aou_attr_vseq
----

first; aou_t1_attr_chk checks each exclusive response is the subordinate's,
and xfer_cov.excl_cg counts EXOKAY and failed exclusives each way.

----
+attr_early=1 enables early write responses on every RP, makes the
----

exclusive accesses bufferable (AWCACHE[0]=1) and the traffic after them
writes only (half bufferable, no sweep): an exclusive write still gets its
real EXOKAY, since only the subordinate can grant it (MAS 3.7.1: AWLOCK=1
is never answered early, whatever AWCACHE[0] and EARLY_ALWAYS_EN say).

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_attr_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/aou_attr_vseq.svh`):

Exclusive accesses end to end (plan 4.25, 5.23), then the data-path traffic
of aou_dp_vseq. With `excl` set, every RP runs, from the local S port and
from the remote die at once, these rounds for each exclusive shape the
narrower of the two buses allows (AXI4 A7.2.4: 2^n bytes up to 128, at most
16 beats, aligned to the total size). Both subordinates (the remote model
and the local memory) keep an exclusive monitor, so the DUT only has to
carry AxLOCK and EXOKAY:
exclusive read A, exclusive write A (same ID)           -> EXOKAY, EXOKAY
exclusive read B, plain write into B, exclusive write B -> EXOKAY, OKAY
exclusive write C with no exclusive read                -> OKAY
aou_t1_attr_chk checks that the requester gets the subordinate's answer
(DP-R07) and xfer_cov counts both outcomes; the scoreboard checks that only
the EXOKAY write changed memory.

*Rules named.* `DP-R07`

*Pass criteria.* The base test's end-of-test checks: scoreboard drained, every declared expectation met, no unexpected `UVM_ERROR`/`UVM_FATAL`, the FDI checker clean; `scripts/check_run.py` judges the log against `expected_fail.yaml`.

----

[[aou-proc-aou_early_bresp_test]]
===== 29. `aou_early_bresp_test`
Class `aou_early_bresp_test` extends `aou_dp_base_test` (`uvm/tests/features/aou_early_bresp_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* Early write response (plan 16.1-16.10, 16.13-16.15, 16.17; old F3, F8).

----
+early_en=0|1|per_rp programs EARLY_BRESP_EN on every RP before activation
----

(per_rp: a random setting per RP, at least one on and one off, 16.15); local writes are
bufferable with +dp_buf_pct probability; +dp_ids=same interleaves bufferable
and non-bufferable writes on one ID. aou_early_bresp_chk checks that only
bufferable writes with the feature on get B before the remote completion.

----
+early_err=1 adds two rounds of a bufferable write the remote die answers
----

with SLVERR, then DECERR: the early OKAY stands, INT_EARLY_RESP_ERR rises and
WRITE_EARLY_RESPONSE_RP0 captures ID and type until W1C (16.4-16.7).

----
+early_full=1 (16.11/16.12): every write bufferable and single-beat, the
----

remote die answers each one +early_lat cycles (default 2000) after it, so
the early table fills to its WR_MO_CNT (32) entries and drains as the
actual B responses arrive; the env's aou_t1_early_tbl_chk checks the AW
stall and its release (FEAT-R15/R16), the vseq WRITE_RESP_DONE once drained.

----
+early_over=1 with +early_full=1 (16.17): the env's early-table checker also
----

reports INT_EARLY_WDT_ERR while an AW waits at the limit (FEAT-R21 is not
checked: O_PENDING_CNT_OVER, BUGS/005, was removed by PR #89 for the watchdog).

----
+early_toggle=1 (16.14): two traffic phases; between them, with every write
----

done and WRITE_RESP_DONE = 1 on every RP (MAS 3.7.8), each RP's
EARLY_BRESP_EN is inverted, and the second phase must follow the new setting.
Writes only, so no read races a write that was answered early.

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_early_bresp_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/aou_early_bresp_vseq.svh`):

Early write response (MAS 3.7). Local writes, bufferable or not, with
EARLY_BRESP_EN programmed before activation (aou_early_bresp_chk checks the
B timing). With err_rounds > 0 it then sends, per round, one bufferable write
into a remote error region (set up by the test) and checks the capture
registers and their W1C clear (FEAT-R07). With early_full the remote die
answers every write early_lat cycles late, so the early table fills, and
once drained every RP's WRITE_RESP_DONE must read 1 (FEAT-R16). With
early_toggle, between the two traffic phases every write is drained,
WRITE_RESP_DONE must read 1 on every RP, and each RP's EARLY_BRESP_EN is
inverted (MAS 3.7.8); the checker judges the second phase by the new value.

*Rules named.* `FEAT-R07`, `FEAT-R15`, `FEAT-R16`, `FEAT-R21`

*Pass criteria.* The base test's end-of-test checks: scoreboard drained, every declared expectation met, no unexpected `UVM_ERROR`/`UVM_FATAL`, the FDI checker clean; `scripts/check_run.py` judges the log against `expected_fail.yaml`.

*Scenarios.*

|===
| Scenario | Arguments | Seeds | Target | Plan items

| `aou_early_bresp_test.early_en-1.dp_buf_pct-50` | `+early_en=1 +dp_buf_pct=50` | 1-3 |  | 16.2,16.3,16.13
| `aou_early_bresp_test.early_en-1.dp_buf_pct-50.dp_ids-same` | `+early_en=1 +dp_buf_pct=50 +dp_ids=same` | 1-2 |  | 16.8,16.9,16.10
| `aou_early_bresp_test.early_en-1.early_err-1` | `+early_en=1 +early_err=1` | 1-2 |  | 16.4,16.5,16.6,16.7

[[aou-proc-aou_pack_test]]
===== 32. `aou_pack_test`
Class `aou_pack_test` extends `aou_dp_base_test` (`uvm/tests/stress/aou_pack_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* Flit packing in both directions (plan 6.3-6.8, 6.14, 6.18-6.21, 11.1, 11.2,
11.5, 11.9, 11.14). The remote die's L3 packer runs non-DUT-like policies;
aou_pack_stats requires the targeted layouts to occur (DP-R01), and the
scoreboard and L3 rule checks judge them. +pk=:
crossflit  every L3 data message longer than split_at (1-7) is forced
across the flit boundary; sizes 256/512/1024 (+remote_bytes)
mixed      sparse layout (holes, random order, mixed credit grants) with
L3 backlog bursts: WriteReq + ReadReq + WriteResp in one flit
single     one message per flit, MsgStart at a random granule 1-18
full       best-fit packing with backlog bursts: flits filled to G47
wresp48    remote reads of nothing but WriteResp backlog: 48 in one flit
rp         multi-RP builds: messages of several RPs in one flit
act        activation cycles with traffic, two zero CrdtGrants per half
crdt       credits only through CrdtGrant messages, plus zero grants
b2b        no idle cycles on FDI either way (trdy always, no gaps)
prof       random PROF (FLEX[11:0]) in AXI messages to the DUT

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_pack_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/stress/aou_pack_vseq.svh`):

Data-path traffic for the packing tests (aou_pack_test, +pk=), with two
twists some modes use: `bursts` makes L3 hold its credited messages back in random windows
while traffic runs, so they leave as dense backlogs (full flits, mixed
types); `act_cycles` deactivates and reactivates the link between traffic
phases, so Activation messages meet traffic and credit grants.

*Rules named.* `DP-R01`

*Pass criteria.* The base test's end-of-test checks: scoreboard drained, every declared expectation met, no unexpected `UVM_ERROR`/`UVM_FATAL`, the FDI checker clean; `scripts/check_run.py` judges the log against `expected_fail.yaml`.

+qos_tiers=3|2|eq|eq01  three RPs on high/normal/low, two RPs on high/low,
----

two RPs on one tier (round-robin among equals), or
two RPs with PRIOR 0 and PRIOR 1 (one tier: 0 reads as 1)

----
+qos_prior0=1        every low-tier RP (tier 1) programmed with PRIOR 0
+qos_timer=off|promote|sweep|thr0|res0|max  starvation timer far beyond
----

the test, short enough to promote the low tier, a
random one of the two, or the extremes: THRESHOLD 0
(promotes at once), RESOLUTION 0 with a short
threshold (promotes), THRESHOLD 0xFFFF (never within
the test)

----
+qos_bounds=1|inv    random AXI_QOS_TO_HP > AXI_QOS_TO_NP, or HP at or
----

below NP (empty Normal tier; arb_mode 2, two tiers)

----
+qos_rounds=N
----

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_qos_order_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/stress/aou_qos_order_vseq.svh`):

QoS arbitration order (MAS 3.2.1, Figures 4-7). Each round holds the DUT's
TX (hold_tx), then issues reads and single-beat writes on each tier's RP,
lowest tier first with `gap` cycles between tiers so the ring buffer and the
lower tiers' queues fill before the higher tiers arrive, releases the TX and
hands the result to aou_qos_order_chk. Tiers: Port QoS (arb_mode 1) maps
RPn_PRIOR 3/2/1 to high/normal/low (Figure 6); AXI QoS (arb_mode 2) takes
each RP's AxQOS against AXI_QOS_TO_HP/NP; round-robin (arb_mode 0, or equal
priorities) puts every RP in one tier.

*Rules named.* `FEAT-R11`

[[aou-proc-aou_link_act_deact_test]]
===== 36. `aou_link_act_deact_test`
Class `aou_link_act_deact_test` extends `aou_base_test` (`uvm/tests/link/aou_link_act_deact_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* Activation/deactivation loops from either side and each CREDIT_MANAGE value
(aou_link_act_deact_vseq).

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_link_act_deact_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/link/aou_link_act_deact_vseq.svh`):

Repeated activation and deactivation with traffic in between (port of
ucie_axi_fdi_aou_flits_test, extended). Each loop activates from the DUT,
the remote die or both (randomized order and gap, simultaneous included),
carries traffic, and deactivates from either side under a CREDIT_MANAGE
value, either idle or with transactions still in flight (MAS §7.3.6:
requests the deactivation caught are answered after a re-activation).
The AOU_INIT status bits are read back at every step.
Knobs: +loops +who=apb|remote|both|rand +order=dut|remote|simul|rand

----
+deact_who=... +credit_manage=0|1 (-1 random per loop) +busy=0|1 (-1 random)
+T1_TXN=<per RP and direction> +force=0|1.
+early_act=1 (plan 1.11; MAS 7.3.2): every activation is software's
----

ACTIVATE_START written while the FDI link is down (at power-on, then after
an Adapter LinkReset). The register reads back 1 with the DUT still DISABLED
until the link comes up (T1-L43); the activation must then start on its own
(T1-V02/T1-V03), and the bit clears itself once ENABLED (T1-L09). The test
keeps the Adapter from bringing the link up after reset.

*Rules named.* `T1-L09`, `T1-L43`, `T1-V02`, `T1-V03`

[[aou-proc-aou_act_after_deact_test]]
===== 38. `aou_act_after_deact_test`
Class `aou_act_after_deact_test` extends `aou_base_test` (`uvm/tests/link/aou_act_after_deact_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* ACTIVATE_START swept across the end of a deactivation (aou_act_after_deact_vseq,
BUGS/020).

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_act_after_deact_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/link/aou_act_after_deact_vseq.svh`):

Software starts activation again just as a deactivation completes
(BUGS/020). The DUT starts the deactivation; the remote die acknowledges
at once but holds its own DeactivateReq until the test releases it, as a
remote die still finishing its own requests would (AoU 8.4). The DUT's
DeactivateAck to that request is then its last message before DISABLED,
and the test writes AOU_INIT.ACTIVATE_START at a swept offset from the
DUT's DISABLED, so the DUT's ActivateReq moves across the flit that carries
the DeactivateAck and the flits after it. A write that lands before
DISABLED is held by the DUT until DISABLED: the MAS allows ACTIVATE_START
before link-up (7.3.2) and activation right after DISABLED (7.3.6) but says
nothing about DEACTIVATE (noted in BUGS/020). The placement of the
Activation messages (one per flit, at G0, AoU 4.4) is judged by AOU-R6 in
the L3 unpacker and AOU_FDI_CHECKER.
The first loop calibrates the APB write time and the delay from the remote
DeactivateReq to the DUT's DISABLED; every later loop aims the end of the
ACTIVATE_START write at DISABLED + offset and logs the offset it got. The
register takes the write about halfway through (26 of 52 cycles on T1).
Knobs: +offsets=<o,o,..> (cycles, may be negative; default -12..44)

----
+busy=0|1 (-1: random per loop) +credit_manage=0|1 +T1_TXN.
----

*Rules named.* `AOU-R6`

*Pass criteria.* The base test's end-of-test checks: scoreboard drained, every declared expectation met, no unexpected `UVM_ERROR`/`UVM_FATAL`, the FDI checker clean; `scripts/check_run.py` judges the log against `expected_fail.yaml`.

[[aou-proc-aou_credit_return_test]]
===== 39. `aou_credit_return_test`
Class `aou_credit_return_test` extends `aou_base_test` (`uvm/tests/link/aou_credit_return_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* Credit advertisement and return corners (aou_credit_return_vseq).

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_credit_return_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/link/aou_credit_return_vseq.svh`):

Credit advertisement and return corners (ports of aou_credit_encoding_test
and aou_msgcredit_encoding_test, extended). Every loop is one activation
epoch with its own remote-die credit setup, chosen before activation:
- initial advertisement per class at an encoded value (Table 17), or a
non-encodable depth that needs several grants;
- return through CrdtGrant only, header MsgCredit only, both mixed in a
flit, or DUT-like (initial grant, then header);
- return immediately, only at RX dequeue, delayed, withheld until a
release (in bursts while traffic runs, so the DUT sees its credit
oscillate);
- optionally over-grants beyond the buffer, which the DUT's counter must
absorb by saturating (§6.4).
Traffic runs both ways; the model checks that the DUT never sends without
credit (AOU-R16) and that its own decoding of the DUT's grants and
MsgCredit lets every transaction finish.
Knobs: +loops +method=dut|hdr|grant|mixed|rand +ret=imm|consume|delayed|
withheld|rand +depth=<granules, all classes> +overgrant=0|1 +T1_TXN.

*Rules named.* `AOU-R16`

*Pass criteria.* The base test's end-of-test checks: scoreboard drained, every declared expectation met, no unexpected `UVM_ERROR`/`UVM_FATAL`, the FDI checker clean; `scripts/check_run.py` judges the log against `expected_fail.yaml`.

[[aou-proc-aou_zero_credit_test]]
===== 40. `aou_zero_credit_test`
Class `aou_zero_credit_test` extends `aou_base_test` (`uvm/tests/link/aou_zero_credit_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* Zero credit for one class, then a late grant (aou_zero_credit_vseq).

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_zero_credit_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/link/aou_zero_credit_vseq.svh`):

Zero credit for one class (port of aou_zero_{wreq,rreq,wdata,rdata,wresp}
_credit_test). The remote die advertises no credit of that class at
activation; traffic that needs it must stay queued in the DUT, never sent
without credit (AOU-R16, checked by the model) and never dropped. After

----
+hold cycles the remote die grants +grant credits and everything completes
----

with correct data.
Knobs: +credit=wreq|rreq|wdata|rdata|wresp (random) +hold=<cycles>

----
+grant=<credits> +T1_TXN=<transactions>.
+starve_rp=<r> (plan 3.15/12.14): only RP r has no credit of the class;
----

traffic runs on every RP, and the others' may complete while RP r's stays
queued.

----
+limit=<k> with +credit=wreq|rreq (plan 8.3/8.6): every RP gets credit for
----

exactly k requests and the remote die returns none of it until released,
with more than k requests queued per RP.
aou_t1_crd_flow_chk judges both in every test: an RP with credit and queued
work keeps sending while another RP has none (T1-C01), the DUT uses all the
credit it holds (T1-C02), never more (AOU-R16, the L3 model).

----
+deact=1 (plan 2.5; MAS 7.3.3): with the traffic still queued for want of
----

credit, software sets DEACTIVATE_START (CREDIT_MANAGE from +credit_manage,
default 0), and the grant comes +deact_hold cycles later. Messages waiting
for credit remain to be transmitted (MAS 7.1), so they must still go out
before the DUT's DeactivateReq (AOU-R34, AOU-R33 in the L3 model; T1-L47 in
aou_t1_rx_fifo_chk for responses to the remote die) and every transaction
completes (scoreboard).

*Rules named.* `AOU-R16`, `AOU-R33`, `AOU-R34`, `T1-C01`, `T1-C02`, `T1-L47`

[[aou-proc-aou_act_rx_drain_test]]
===== 41. `aou_act_rx_drain_test`
Class `aou_act_rx_drain_test` extends `aou_base_test` (`uvm/tests/link/aou_act_rx_drain_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* Re-activation with remote requests still in the DUT's RX FIFO
(aou_act_rx_drain_vseq).

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_act_rx_drain_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/link/aou_act_rx_drain_vseq.svh`):

Stimulus for activation with data in the RX FIFO (plan 1.10; MAS 7.3.2,
7.3.4). The scenario MAS 7.3.4 and 7.3.5 describe, with CREDIT_MANAGE=0: the
remote die's requests cross the DUT's DeactivateReq, the remote die then
deactivates with them unanswered (they are answered after the next
activation), and the DUT's M ports hold AWREADY, WREADY and ARREADY low, so
the requests are still in its RX FIFOs when the link reaches DISABLED.
Software sets ACTIVATE_START and the M ports stay held for +hold cycles,
then drain; activation follows and every held request completes.
aou_t1_rx_fifo_chk checks that the DUT's ActivateReq waits for the FIFO
(T1-L40) and its credit for what is still queued (T1-C41).
Knobs: +hold=<cycles> +loops +T1_TXN=<per RP>.

*Rules named.* `T1-C41`, `T1-L40`

[[aou-proc-aou_rx_credit_test]]
===== 42. `aou_rx_credit_test`
Class `aou_rx_credit_test` extends `aou_base_test` (`uvm/tests/link/aou_rx_credit_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* The DUT's advertised RX credit against its FIFO depths, and credit held while
the M port back-pressures (aou_rx_credit_vseq).

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_rx_credit_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/link/aou_rx_credit_vseq.svh`):

Stimulus for the DUT's RX credit (plan 3.20, 3.23, 3.25; MAS 3.4, 3.9).
Every loop is one activation epoch: the DUT advertises its credit, then
(+bp=1) every M port holds AWREADY, WREADY and ARREADY low for +hold cycles
while the remote die sends writes and reads, so they queue in the DUT's RX
FIFOs; the ports are released, traffic runs both ways and drains, and the
link deactivates. A last activation ends the test quiescent in ENABLED.
The checks are passive: aou_l3_model (T1-C40: never more credit than the
MAS 3.9 maximum for the RP's RX FIFO depth and width, and all of it once
quiescent) and aou_t1_rx_fifo_chk (T1-C41: credit for messages still in the
RX FIFO stays with the DUT). The -rxf configuration builds the DUT with
non-default FIFO depths and the RX FIFO register slices off (3.25).
Knobs: +loops +hold=<cycles> +bp=0|1 +T1_TXN=<remote transactions per RP
while held>.

*Rules named.* `T1-C40`, `T1-C41`

*Pass criteria.* The base test's end-of-test checks: scoreboard drained, every declared expectation met, no unexpected `UVM_ERROR`/`UVM_FATAL`, the FDI checker clean; `scripts/check_run.py` judges the log against `expected_fail.yaml`.

[[aou-proc-aou_deact_ctrl_test]]
===== 43. `aou_deact_ctrl_test`
Class `aou_deact_ctrl_test` extends `aou_base_test` (`uvm/tests/link/aou_deact_ctrl_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* AOU_INIT deactivation controls: the DEACTIVATE_TIME_OUT_VALUE gate and
INT_DEACTIVATE_PROPERTY (aou_deact_ctrl_vseq, +mode=tov|property).

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_deact_ctrl_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/link/aou_deact_ctrl_vseq.svh`):

Deactivation controls in AOU_INIT.

----
+mode=tov (plan 2.12; MAS 7.1 AOU_INIT.DEACTIVATE_TIME_OUT_VALUE): for each
----

value v in +tov_values (default 0..7, shuffled) the remote die starts a few
reads and software sets DEACTIVATE_START (CREDIT_MANAGE=1) +0..200 cycles
later, so the DUT's last ReadData lands near the deactivation and its
DeactivateReq has to wait out the 2^(v+3)-cycle quiet window behind it.
aou_t1_rx_fifo_chk checks the window on every DeactivateReq (T1-L46; the
quiet-window reading is the BUGS/057 interim).

----
+mode=property (plan 2.10; BUGS/010, which covers the bit too): the remote
----

die deactivates with PropertyReq 0 and 1 (+prop fixes it). Software holds
off DEACTIVATE_START, so the DUT stays in DEACTIVATE while the test reads
INT_DEACTIVATE_PROPERTY back: the PropertyReq received, and 0 before any
DeactivateReq and again in the next ENABLED epoch (T1-L45, interim
expectation). Its value once DISABLED is only logged.

*Rules named.* `T1-L45`, `T1-L46`

[[aou-proc-aou_invalid_actmsg_test]]
===== 44. `aou_invalid_actmsg_test`
Class `aou_invalid_actmsg_test` extends `aou_base_test` (`uvm/tests/errors/aou_invalid_actmsg_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* Activation messages in the wrong state, LinkReset and recovery (aou_invalid_actmsg_vseq).

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_invalid_actmsg_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/errors/aou_invalid_actmsg_vseq.svh`):

Activation messages in the wrong state (ports of
ucie_axi_fdi_invalid_msgs_test and _en2dis_test, extended to every state
and opcode). The DUT is held in DISABLED, ACTIVATE (its ActivateReq not
answered), ENABLED or DEACTIVATE (its DeactivateReq not answered), and the
remote die sends one opcode regardless of state. MAS §7.2.3 says which
opcodes are invalid in each state; for those the DUT sets
INVALID_ACTMSG_ERR, captures the opcode in INVALID_ACTMSG_INFO, raises
INT_REQ_LINKRESET (unless masked, BUGS/014) and acknowledges an invalid
ActivateReq but not an invalid ActivateAck (#78/#79). Software then
recovers (LinkReset, AOU_SW_RESET, re-activation) and traffic must work.
Opcodes the MAS permits but the spec calls inconsistent (BUGS/013) must
not raise LinkReset, and the link must still work afterwards.
The Ack to an invalid ActivateReq must be on FDI before lp_linkerror rises
(T1-L30, aou_t1_act_chk, for every ActivateReq in every test); +reps and
the pl_trdy knobs give it Acks that can still sit in the DUT's TX stage.
Knobs: +state=disabled|activate|enabled|deactivate|all +op=act_req|act_ack|
deact_req|deact_ack|all +mask=0|1 +reps=N (each case N times, default 1)

----
+T1_TXN.
----

*Rules named.* `T1-L30`

[[aou-proc-aou_linkreset_timeout_test]]
===== 45. `aou_linkreset_timeout_test`
Class `aou_linkreset_timeout_test` extends `aou_base_test` (`uvm/tests/errors/aou_linkreset_timeout_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* Ack and MsgCredit time-outs, LinkReset and recovery (aou_linkreset_timeout_vseq).

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_linkreset_timeout_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/errors/aou_linkreset_timeout_vseq.svh`):

The three time-out LinkReset sources (MAS §7.2.3; plan 1.3, 2.6, 3.18):
act_ack:   the remote die never answers the DUT's ActivateReq;
deact_ack: it never answers the DUT's DeactivateReq;
msgcredit: it completes activation but never sends a CrdtGrant.
The time-out is shortened through its register (+tmo, 2^(tmo+18) cycles).
The sticky bit must still be clear shortly before the time-out and set
after it, with INT_REQ_LINKRESET unless the source is masked (BUGS/014).
Software then recovers and traffic must work.
Knobs: +src=act_ack|deact_ack|msgcredit|rand +mask=0|1 +tmo=0..7.

[[aou-proc-aou_rx_msg_error_test]]
===== 46. `aou_rx_msg_error_test`
Class `aou_rx_msg_error_test` extends `aou_base_test` (`uvm/tests/errors/aou_rx_msg_error_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* Malformed messages from the remote die (aou_rx_msg_error_vseq).

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_rx_msg_error_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/errors/aou_rx_msg_error_vseq.svh`):

Malformed messages from the remote die, one kind per case, between bursts
of checked traffic. The spec defines no receiver reaction (BUGS/012); the
interim expectation is that the DUT drops what it cannot decode, raises
no interrupt and no LinkReset, and later traffic completes with correct
data. Each injection must be reported by the testbench's own checkers
(the model's TX decode and AOU_FDI_CHECKER), which proves it reached the
wire.
bad_type    reserved MSGTYPE 0111b..1111b          AOU-R3
bad_miscop  reserved MISCOP                         AOU-R3
bad_actop   reserved ACTIVATIONOP                   AOU-R3
bad_dlength WriteData with DLENGTH=11b              AOU-R3
rsvd        CrdtGrant (no credit) with RsvdZero17   AOU-R11
flip_start  MsgStart set inside a CrdtGrant         AOU-R4
rp_range    WriteResp naming RP >= RP_COUNT         AOU-R14
hdr_rp      header MsgCredit naming RP >= RP_COUNT  AOU-R14
grant_rp    CrdtGrant crediting an RP >= RP_COUNT   AOU-R11
fdid        an empty flit with FDId 1               AOU-R9
hdr_rsvd    an empty flit with protocol-header      AOU-R1
RsvdZero bits set
RP-range kinds need RP_COUNT < 4 and are skipped otherwise.
Knobs: +kind=<one of the above>|all +T1_TXN.

*Rules named.* `AOU-R1`, `AOU-R11`, `AOU-R14`, `AOU-R3`, `AOU-R4`, `AOU-R9`

[[aou-proc-aou_slv_id_mismatch_test]]
===== 47. `aou_slv_id_mismatch_test`
Class `aou_slv_id_mismatch_test` extends `aou_base_test` (`uvm/tests/errors/aou_slv_id_mismatch_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* Subordinate-side ID mismatch on every RP (aou_slv_id_mismatch_vseq). No
traffic: only unsolicited responses from the remote die.

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_slv_id_mismatch_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/errors/aou_slv_id_mismatch_vseq.svh`):

Subordinate-side AXI ID mismatch on every RP (plan 9.11, 9.12; main #76).
The remote die answers a request the DUT never sent: a WriteResp (BID) or
a ReadData (RID) whose ID has nothing pending on that RP. Per RP and kind:
T1-E16  AXI_SLV_ID_MISMATCH_ERR_RPn sets the error bit of that kind with
the ID in its INFO field; no other RP or kind is set;
T1-E17  INT_SI0_ID_MISMATCH rises (MAS 7.2.2) and falls after the W1C;
T1-E18  white-box: of AOU_CORE's two aggregates that AOU_CORE_TOP ORs
into INT_SI0_ID_MISMATCH, only the one of that kind is set. At
the DUT's ports the two are indistinguishable, so this is the
only place #76 (RP1-RP3 crossed) shows.
The checker is enabled through bit 22 of AXI_SLV_ID_MISMATCH_ERR_RPn, which
the RDL calls reserved and the MAS says is tied off (BUGS/003 interim:
the bit enables the checker; the #76 commit describes the per-RP bits and
aggregates).
Knobs: +kind=b|r|both (default both) +id=<hex>.

*Rules named.* `T1-E16`, `T1-E17`, `T1-E18`

*Pass criteria.* The base test's end-of-test checks: scoreboard drained, every declared expectation met, no unexpected `UVM_ERROR`/`UVM_FATAL`, the FDI checker clean; `scripts/check_run.py` judges the log against `expected_fail.yaml`.

[[aou-proc-aou_axi_err_resp_test]]
===== 48. `aou_axi_err_resp_test`
Class `aou_axi_err_resp_test` extends `aou_base_test` (`uvm/tests/errors/aou_axi_err_resp_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* AXI error responses both ways and the response error debug FIFO
(aou_axi_err_resp_vseq).

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_axi_err_resp_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/errors/aou_axi_err_resp_vseq.svh`):

AXI error responses on both sides and the R/B response error debug FIFO
(plan 9.1, 9.2, 9.13, 9.14; MAS software-operation 7.2.4).

fifo (every RP at once): software enables remote access to each RP's FIFO
at its own debug address before activation. The remote die's writes and
reads into local SLVERR/DECERR regions come back with that response
(scoreboard) and each pushes {ID, ADDR, RESP}; the remote die reads the
head entry at the debug address and pops it with a write there
(aou_t1_dbg_fifo_chk checks every read and pop):
- one B error, then one R error;
- six errors in a row, four pops, one more error: the fifth and sixth
meet a full FIFO;
- a B error and an R error issued 0..7 cycles apart, so some land in the
same cycle (two pushes at once).
resp (every RP, both directions): single and burst writes and reads into
SLVERR/DECERR regions, bursts that run from one region into the other or
into OKAY memory; every beat's response must reach the requester unchanged.
split (plan 15.11, 15.13; run with the limits below under 15): the remote
die's 16-beat bursts into local memory, which the RP splits, each touching
32-byte error regions that fall in one M-port beat and so one sub-burst
(first, middle or last; two, SLVERR and DECERR, in the fourth). The merged
BRESP must be the worst of the sub-burst responses and each remote R beat
the worst of the M-port beats it is built from (AXI4 A3.4.4 and MAS 3.6),
which is what the scoreboard expects from the error regions.
Then ordinary traffic must still complete.
Knobs:

----
+part=all|fifo|resp|split
+max_awburstlen=N +max_arburstlen=N  MAX_AxBURSTLEN (AxLEN, 2^n-1)
----

programmed on every RP before activation; with +part=fifo
debug accesses longer than N+1 RP beats meet the splitter
(BUGS/043).

----
+dbg_len=N|max  AxLEN of every debug-window read and pop (default 0, one
----

beat; max: the longest burst inside the 4 KB window).

*Pass criteria.* The base test's end-of-test checks: scoreboard drained, every declared expectation met, no unexpected `UVM_ERROR`/`UVM_FATAL`, the FDI checker clean; `scripts/check_run.py` judges the log against `expected_fail.yaml`.

[[aou-proc-aou_before_enable_test]]
===== 49. `aou_before_enable_test`
Class `aou_before_enable_test` extends `aou_base_test` (`uvm/tests/errors/aou_before_enable_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* AXI requests before AoU activation (aou_before_enable_vseq).

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_before_enable_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/errors/aou_before_enable_vseq.svh`):

AXI requests before AoU activation (plan 9.6). With the link up but AoU
DISABLED the DUT has no credits and may send only ActivateReq (AoU 8.4;
MAS 7.3.1), so local requests must wait: none completes and no request
reaches the remote die (its L3 checker and AOU_FDI_CHECKER would report a
credited message outside ENABLED). A request waiting to be sent raises
INT_ACTIVATE_START (MAS 7.3.5, condition 1); the local software is held
off, so the interrupt must stay set until software activates. Once both
dies are ENABLED every request completes with correct data.
Knobs: +hold=<cycles to wait before activating> (default 500..3000).

*Pass criteria.* The base test's end-of-test checks: scoreboard drained, every declared expectation met, no unexpected `UVM_ERROR`/`UVM_FATAL`, the FDI checker clean; `scripts/check_run.py` judges the log against `expected_fail.yaml`.

[[aou-proc-aou_credit_violation_test]]
===== 50. `aou_credit_violation_test`
Class `aou_credit_violation_test` extends `aou_base_test` (`uvm/tests/errors/aou_credit_violation_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* ReadReqs beyond the DUT's advertised credit (aou_credit_violation_vseq).

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_credit_violation_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/errors/aou_credit_violation_vseq.svh`):

The remote die sends ReadReqs beyond the RREQ credit the DUT advertised
(inject("no_credit"); plan 9.5). AoU 6.1 forbids it; neither the spec nor
the MAS says what the receiver does (BUGS/030). Interim expectation:
- the testbench's checkers see the violation on the wire (AOU-R16);
- the DUT raises no interrupt and no LinkReset (the MAS lists no credit
overflow error) and stays ENABLED;
- every ReadReq within the credit is answered with correct data
(scoreboard); one beyond it is either answered correctly or dropped,
never answered wrongly or twice;
- after software's LinkReset recovery (MAS 7.3.6), which ends any read
still waiting, traffic completes both ways.
The M port's ARREADY is held low meanwhile and the reads go out without an
outstanding limit (the test lifts it), so the DUT fills whatever it buffers
behind its RX credit and stops returning credit; the reads sent while the
remote die holds no credit are the violations (AOU-R16, one per read).
Knobs: +extra=<ReadReqs beyond the credit> (default 1..8).

*Rules named.* `AOU-R16`

[[aou-proc-aou_id_mismatch_test]]
===== 51. `aou_id_mismatch_test`
Class `aou_id_mismatch_test` extends `aou_base_test` (`uvm/tests/errors/aou_id_mismatch_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* AXI ID mismatch on the M and S ports, every RP (aou_id_mismatch_vseq).

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_id_mismatch_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/errors/aou_id_mismatch_vseq.svh`):

AXI ID mismatch on both sides, on every RP (plan 9.9-9.12, 19.7, 19.8;
MAS software-operation 7.2.2, interrupts-errors 4).

mgr: with nothing outstanding, the local subordinate on RP r's M port
returns a B, then a one-beat R, whose ID matches no request. The DUT must
take it (interim, BUGS/029: accept and drop it), set ERROR_INFO_RPr
SPLIT_BID/RID_MISMATCH_ERR with the ID in the INFO field and raise
INT_MI0_ID_MISMATCH.
sub: the remote die sends a WriteResp, then a ReadData, for no request of
RP r. With the subordinate checker enabled (AXI_SLV_ID_MISMATCH_ERR_RPr bit
22, which the RDL calls reserved: BUGS/003 interim) the DUT must keep it off
the S port, set AXI_SLV_BID/RID_MISMATCH_ERR with the ID and raise
INT_SI0_ID_MISMATCH. With it disabled (+slv_en=0) nothing is recorded (MAS
7.2.2) and the response must still stay off the S port.
With +mask=1 the interrupt mask is set first: the status bit is still set
but the interrupt stays low until the mask is cleared (interim, BUGS/029:
interrupt = status & ~mask). Write 1 clears the error, its INFO and the
interrupt. Traffic must complete afterwards.
The orphan stays on the M port until taken (AXI4 forbids withdrawing it);
when the DUT does not take it, or lets an unrequested response through to
the S port, the test reports that and pulses I_RESETN/I_PRESETN, the only
legal way to end it, before going on.

----
+detect_only=1 (M port only) is a bug-avoiding variant for BUGS/029: after
----

the orphan it checks the status, INFO, interrupt and mask, then ends the
scenario with a hard reset instead of the write-1 clear and more traffic.
It does not check that the DUT takes the orphan within accept_wait cycles,
which is the 029 interim expectation itself, so it is weaker than the
default run and never replaces it (coverage-closure decision D8).
Knobs: +side=all|mgr|sub +kind=all|b|r +mask=0|1 +slv_en=0|1 +detect_only=0|1.

*Pass criteria.* The base test's end-of-test checks: scoreboard drained, every declared expectation met, no unexpected `UVM_ERROR`/`UVM_FATAL`, the FDI checker clean; `scripts/check_run.py` judges the log against `expected_fail.yaml`.

[[aou-proc-aou_int_test]]
===== 52. `aou_int_test`
Class `aou_int_test` extends `aou_base_test` (`uvm/tests/errors/aou_int_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* Interrupt status, masks and write-1-to-clear (aou_int_vseq).

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_int_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/errors/aou_int_vseq.svh`):

Interrupt status, masks and write-1-to-clear (plan 19.5, 19.9, 19.11,
19.12; MAS interrupts-errors 4, software-operation 7.1/7.2). Modes:
w1c   (old aou_int_w1c_test) the local software is off. A remote
ActivateReq sets INT_ACTIVATE_START and a remote DeactivateReq
INT_DEACTIVATE_START; reading them or writing 0 leaves them (and the
interrupt) set, writing 1 clears them. Then an ActivateAck in
ENABLED sets LP_LINKRESET.INVALID_ACTMSG_ERR, which behaves the same
and takes INVALID_ACTMSG_INFO with it; the link is recovered.
early every RP gets a bufferable write whose remote completion is an
error at the same time: early OKAY, then WRITE_RESP_ERR with ID and
type, and INT_EARLY_RESP_ERR until the last RP is cleared. +mask=1
sets INT_EARLY_RESP_MASK: status still set, interrupt low until the
mask is cleared (interim, BUGS/029).
multi on every RP at once an early-response error and a WriteResp
nobody asked for (subordinate checker on, BUGS/003), then an
ActivateAck in ENABLED (LinkReset). All three interrupts and every
status bit are set; clearing one source leaves the others; the link
is recovered. (An M-port ID mismatch cannot join: BUGS/029.)
race  a write-1-to-clear of WRITE_RESP_ERR swept across the cycle a new
early-response error sets it: the new error must never be lost
(interim, BUGS/029: a set in the clearing cycle wins).
Knobs: +mode=all|w1c|early|multi|race +mask=0|1 +race_span=<cycles>.

The remote die answers the first +wide_n=N (default 4) reads of each RP
narrower than 1024 bits with ReadData1024; the reads are single and short
bursts of the full RP width.

Class `aou_lp_mode_traffic_test` extends `aou_base_test` (`uvm/tests/lifecycle/aou_lp_mode_traffic_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* TX low-power mode and heartbeat with traffic (aou_lp_mode_traffic_vseq).

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_lp_mode_traffic_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/lifecycle/aou_lp_mode_traffic_vseq.svh`):

TX low-power mode with traffic (MAS §7.1 "Low Power mode"; plan 21.2-21.7).
DUT flits are counted over an idle window after the link settles:
TX_LP_MODE=0                 flits keep flowing: at least a quarter of
the flit slots (the L1 model inserts trdy
holes);
TX_LP_MODE=1, threshold 0    fully gated: no flit while idle;
TX_LP_MODE=1, threshold T    a heartbeat: at least one flit and at most
ceil(W / max(T+1, flit cycles)) + 1
(BUGS/017 interim).
Traffic both ways runs in LP mode, so the remote side completes only if the
DUT still returns credits (21.6), and the mode is switched on and off
mid-traffic (21.7).
Knobs: +threshold=0..255 (random, 0 one time in three) +T1_TXN.

[[aou-proc-aou_lp_mode_align_test]]
===== 55. `aou_lp_mode_align_test`
Class `aou_lp_mode_align_test` extends `aou_base_test` (`uvm/tests/lifecycle/aou_lp_mode_align_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* TX_LP_MODE written on the edge a flit's first half-chunk goes out, with a
message waiting for the next cycle (aou_lp_mode_align_vseq, BUGS/034). The
Adapter keeps pl_trdy high, and the remote die uses PHY0, the half-width
path of the two-PHY builds.

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_lp_mode_align_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/lifecycle/aou_lp_mode_align_vseq.svh`):

TX_LP_MODE switched on at the edge where the lower half of a flit's first
chunk goes out on a half-width FDI path (BUGS/034; MAS software-operation
7.1 "Low Power mode": once a flit is started it always finishes). On
SP_32B, and on PHY0 of the two-PHY builds, a 64- or 128-byte packing chunk
leaves as two FDI beats, so the DUT has to keep the flit going between
them even when the write makes it idle, and must not let a new message into
that chunk.

Each step, with pl_trdy high on every cycle the Adapter allows it:
1. TX_LP_MODE=0, so the DUT sends empty flits back to back;
2. pl_trdy is held low at a flit boundary, so the DUT waits on beat 0
(chunk 0, lower half) of an empty flit;
3. a local write to remote memory is started; it waits in the DUT behind
the held TX, ready to enter the very next chunk;
4. an APB read ends on a pclk edge, then TX_LP_MODE=1 with threshold 0 is
written while pl_trdy returns `off` core cycles later, so beat 0
transfers on one fixed edge relative to the register write;
5. the write must complete and the link must drain.
`off` sweeps a range that holds the edge where the register takes effect,
so one step makes LP mode engage on exactly the beat-0 edge with the
write's message waiting for the next cycle. Any bubble inside the flit is
FDI-R02; a message that enters the half-sent chunk corrupts the flit (L3
and AOU_FDI_CHECKER), or the write is lost (T1-V06) or wrong (scoreboard).
The sweep stops at the first error.
Knobs: +align_min=N +align_max=N (core cycles, default 0..63).

*Rules named.* `FDI-R02`, `T1-V06`

*Pass criteria.* The base test's end-of-test checks: scoreboard drained, every declared expectation met, no unexpected `UVM_ERROR`/`UVM_FATAL`, the FDI checker clean; `scripts/check_run.py` judges the log against `expected_fail.yaml`.

[[aou-proc-aou_reset_test]]
===== 56. `aou_reset_test`
Class `aou_reset_test` extends `aou_base_test` (`uvm/tests/lifecycle/aou_reset_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* Software and hard resets mid-traffic, mid-activation and with queued messages (aou_reset_vseq).

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_reset_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/lifecycle/aou_reset_vseq.svh`):

Resets at awkward moments, then recovery and traffic (plan 11.10-11.12,
11.15). The DUT is first programmed away from its reset values; each loop
picks a reset and a moment:

----
+reset  sw    AOU_SW_RESET inside the MAS LinkReset sequence (BUGS/007
----

interim: every register returns to its reset value)
core  I_RESETN only     } BUGS/016 interim: the registers are on
apb   I_PRESETN only    } the core reset, so they return to their
both  both resets       } reset values on I_RESETN and keep their
} values on I_PRESETN alone

----
+when   idle, traffic (transactions in flight), activating (in the
----

middle of the activation handshake), queued (DUT TX queue held
non-empty by zero WREQ credit).
After the reset software checks the registers, reprograms, brings the
link up and activates; in-flight transactions count as aborted and all
later traffic must complete with correct data.
Knobs: +reset=sw|core|apb|both|rand +when=idle|traffic|activating|queued|
rand +loops +T1_TXN.

[[aou-proc-aou_dft_scan_test]]
===== 57. `aou_dft_scan_test`
Class `aou_dft_scan_test` extends `aou_base_test` (`uvm/tests/lifecycle/aou_dft_scan_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* DFT scan mode and the software reset path (aou_dft_scan_vseq, plan 11.19).

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_dft_scan_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/lifecycle/aou_dft_scan_vseq.svh`):

DFT scan mode (plan 11.19). TIEL_DFT_MODESCAN=1 switches the core reset mux to
its scan input, which the integration guide (3.13.1) says de-asserts the
software reset so that scan shifting is not disturbed: the core comes out of
any software reset and AOU_SW_RESET has no effect while scan mode lasts.
Sequence: traffic; the link goes to Reset as for a software reset; a marker
value goes into a configuration register; scan mode on; the marker must
survive (T1-DFT02, register read-backs at the end of each step), also after an
AOU_SW_RESET write; scan mode off; a hard reset and traffic again. The core
reset itself is judged by aou_t1_sw_reset_chk (T1-DFT01) whenever scan mode is on.
The interim expectation follows the guide's text; the RTL ties the scan input
to 0 (BUGS/052).

*Rules named.* `T1-DFT01`, `T1-DFT02`

*Pass criteria.* The base test's end-of-test checks: scoreboard drained, every declared expectation met, no unexpected `UVM_ERROR`/`UVM_FATAL`, the FDI checker clean; `scripts/check_run.py` judges the log against `expected_fail.yaml`.

[[aou-proc-aou_mrp_test]]
===== 58. `aou_mrp_test`
Class `aou_mrp_test` extends `aou_dp_base_test` (`uvm/tests/matrix/aou_mrp_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* Multi-RP traffic (plan 2.12): aou_mrp_vseq's scenarios with aou_mrp_chk's
per-RP accounting (T1-M01, the per-RP statistics of 12.19), arbitration
(T1-M02) and independence (T1-M03) checks. Both directions, every size up
to each side's width, 1-16 beats. +mrp_scn=crd_rr opens round-robin credit
windows for the env's aou_t1_crd_rr_chk (T1-C03).

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_mrp_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/matrix/aou_mrp_vseq.svh`):

Multi-RP scenarios (plan 2.12) over the RPs in +mrp_rps (default: all),
both directions, data-checked by the scoreboard. +mrp_scn:
solo       traffic on the listed RPs only, the others idle (12.1-12.4)
seq        one RP after another, in list order (12.5, 12.7)
interleave every listed RP at once, back to back, with an arbitration
window on aou_mrp_chk (12.6, 12.8)
indep      +mrp_slow (default: last listed) gets slow local agents while the
others run at full rate (independence window); then all at once
crd_rr     +mrp_loops rounds: with the DUT's TX held, remote-die requests
on a random subset of the listed RPs (all of them in round 0)
leave the DUT owing each of them credit; on release
a window opened on the env's aou_t1_crd_rr_chk has it check the
MsgCredit order (round robin, 3.19)

*Rules named.* `T1-C03`, `T1-M01`, `T1-M02`, `T1-M03`

*Pass criteria.* The base test's end-of-test checks: scoreboard drained, every declared expectation met, no unexpected `UVM_ERROR`/`UVM_FATAL`, the FDI checker clean; `scripts/check_run.py` judges the log against `expected_fail.yaml`.

*Purpose.* [NEG] Duplicate DEST_RP values (plan 12.12, MAS 3.10.3): RP1 is mapped to
the same remote plane as RP0, the remote die's map is the identity. The MAS
says nothing detects it: no interrupt or error is flagged, and credits for a
remote plane no local RP maps to fall to RP0's view (silent credit
accounting errors). Traffic both ways on RP0, RP2 and RP3 (RP1 idle: its
responses could not reach it). Checked: AXI messages carry the programmed
DEST_RP (FEAT-R09, so RP0 and RP1 share a plane), data end to end, no
interrupt; a DUT message beyond its credit (AOU-R16) is allowed, as the MAS
describes. Needs 4 RPs.

[[aou-proc-aou_dest_rp_asym_test]]
===== 60. `aou_dest_rp_asym_test`
Class `aou_dest_rp_asym_test` extends `aou_dest_rp_test` (`uvm/tests/matrix/aou_dest_rp_asym_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* As the procedure below.

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_dest_rp_asym_vseq` (`uvm/tests/matrix/aou_dest_rp_asym_test.svh`):

[NEG] Asymmetric DEST_RP between the dies (plan 12.13). The DUT maps RP0 to
remote plane 1 and RP1 to plane 0; the remote die keeps the identity map,
so it answers a request from the DUT's RP0 on plane 1. MAS 3.10.1 requires
symmetry and says nothing of the result (BUGS/031). Interim expectation:
the DUT tags its requests with its own DEST_RP (FEAT-R09); RP0's reads and
writes never complete at the S port (T1-M04); and no response reaches an S
port with no request outstanding on that ID (AXI4 A5.3: RP1 would report
AXI-R07/R08). After the wait the test abandons the stuck transactions.

*Rules named.* `AXI-R07`, `FEAT-R09`, `T1-M04`

[[aou-proc-aou_perf_test]]
===== 63. `aou_perf_test`
Class `aou_perf_test` extends `aou_dp_base_test` (`uvm/tests/matrix/aou_perf_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* Performance (plan 2.10): aou_perf_vseq's windows (+perf_scn=S1..S5, or

----
+perf_mode=lat|bw|drain) measured by aou_perf_mon into perf.txt and
----

perf.json (docs/PERF_JSON.md) in the run directory. aou_perf_chk gates every
bandwidth window against the committed d2d_model targets (T1-P02..P04); the
latency and drain windows are report only. The scoreboard still checks every
byte. aou_perf_seq replaces the random traffic with each window's exact
pattern. scripts/perf_report.py tabulates the runs.
The env knobs a seed would otherwise pick and that change the traffic shape
are fixed, so every seed and simulator measures the same bench:

----
+perf_r_interleave=0|1 (local subordinates interleave R beats across IDs,
----

default 0), +perf_w_before_aw=0|1 (default 1), +perf_resp_fork=0|1 (remote
responder serves requests concurrently, default 0).
The remote die sends every full-strobe write beat as WriteDataFull
(+perf_remote_full_pct=<pct>, default 100), as the DUT does.
Managers keep +perf_slots outstanding (default 32): with the drivers'
default 16 the remote die's reads could not cover their round trip when
both sides read, and the bench, not the DUT, set the rate.
The remote die advertises enough credit that it is never the limit (the
DUT's counters hold 2048 per class); +perf_l3_depth=env keeps the env's
smaller defaults.

*Procedure.* Virtual sequence `aou_perf_vseq` (`uvm/seq_lib/matrix/aou_perf_vseq.svh`):

Performance windows (plan 2.10) for aou_perf_mon, with no added delay in
any local agent or the remote model. Stimulus only: aou_perf_chk judges the
bandwidth windows against uvm/env/perf/aou_perf_targets.svh.

----
+perf_scn=<S1..S5>  the windows of that scenario on this CONFIG
----

(docs/perf_scenarios.yaml, generated into aou_perf_windows): per RP
and issuing side a whole number of periods of the window's pattern,
sized so every link with data carries at least +perf_kb=<KB>
(default 768) of payload, or +perf_n=<n> periods. aou_perf_seq pins
every shape choice (10.1-10.3, 10.8, 10.10-10.13; credit return
delay 10.6 over the whole run).

----
+perf_mode:
----

lat    one transaction in flight at a time on RP0: writes, then reads, each
way (10.4, 10.5, 10.9; round trip split at FDI)
bw     S1's both-sides windows bw_wr, bw_rd, bw_mix; with +perf_dir=l2r|r2l
S1's one-sided windows of that side instead.
drain  the remote die advertises no ReadReq credit; local reads queue in
the DUT; then one grant per RP releases them (10.7)

----
+perf_slots=<n> sets the transactions each manager keeps outstanding
----

(default 32; see aou_perf_test).

*Rules named.* `T1-P02`

*Pass criteria.* The base test's end-of-test checks: scoreboard drained, every declared expectation met, no unexpected `UVM_ERROR`/`UVM_FATAL`, the FDI checker clean; `scripts/check_run.py` judges the log against `expected_fail.yaml`.

*Purpose.* Walks a 1 and a 0 through every bit of every register (uvm_reg_bit_bash_seq).

fields with no reset value and the self-clearing controls ACTIVATE_START,
DEACTIVATE_START and DEACTIVATE_FORCE (the bash writes them as 0). W1C flags
are bashed: writing 1 to a clear flag must leave it 0.

[[aou-proc-aou_l3_inject_test]]
===== 75. `aou_l3_inject_test`
Class `aou_l3_inject_test` extends `aou_l3_unit_env_test` (`uvm/tests/l3_unit/aou_l3_inject_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* One error injected by model B (the remote die) after legal traffic, chosen
by +L3_INJECT. Each must be caught under the expected rule by the
receiving model A and by AOU_FDI_CHECKER, and, where the error is
structural, by B's own stimulus self-check:
bad_type   reserved MSGTYPE           AOU-R3  (A, B self-check, checker)
rsvd       WriteResp RsvdZero set     AOU-R11 (A, B self-check, checker)
no_credit  WriteResps beyond credit   AOU-R16 (A, checker)
act_seq    ActivateAck in ENABLED     AOU-R40 (A, checker)
msgstart   MsgStart inside a message  AOU-R4  (A, B self-check, checker)
fdid       wrong FDId                 AOU-R9  (A, B self-check, checker)
act_place  Activation not at G0       AOU-R6  (A, B self-check, checker)
overgrant  credit beyond any buffer   saturation in A, AOU-R21 (checker)

*Procedure.* The class's own `run_phase` (see the file).

*Rules named.* `AOU-R11`, `AOU-R16`, `AOU-R21`, `AOU-R3`, `AOU-R4`, `AOU-R40`, `AOU-R6`, `AOU-R9`

[[aou-proc-aou_l3_link_test]]
===== 76. `aou_l3_link_test`
Class `aou_l3_link_test` extends `aou_l3_unit_base_test` (`uvm/tests/l3_unit/aou_l3_link_test.svh`).

*Purpose.* Link controller, two models back to back without time. Legal sequences:
one-sided and simultaneous activation, deactivation from either side,
re-activation with fresh credits. Illegal ones, each with its rule: an
out-of-sequence Ack or Req (AOU-R40), a reserved opcode (AOU-R3), credits
before ActivateAck (AOU-R29), credited traffic in DISABLED (AOU-R26), a
DeactivateReq with requests unanswered (AOU-R33, with the requests that
crossed our own DeactivateReq counted apart), a request after DeactivateReq
(AOU-R34), and v0.8's ERROR state with its recovery.

*Procedure.* The class's own `run_phase` (see the file).

*Rules named.* `AOU-R26`, `AOU-R29`, `AOU-R3`, `AOU-R33`, `AOU-R34`, `AOU-R40`

bus: transactions are fed to the scoreboard directly. A reset_outstanding
